intro: With «se» you speak of nobody in particular: signs, rules and customs.
p.se habla.consejo: The language is the subject: «se habla español», «se hablan dos lenguas».
p.se vende.consejo: With one thing: «se vende un piso». With several: «se venden pisos».
p.se venden.consejo: The final n marks the plural and agrees with what is sold: «se venden coches».
p.se alquila.consejo: The qu sounds like k: al-KI-la. A sign says «se alquila piso».
p.se puede.consejo: «¿Se puede?» is used to ask permission. An infinitive follows: «se puede entrar».
p.se dice que.consejo: It does not say who speaks. A sentence follows «que»: «se dice que va a llover».
p.se necesita.consejo: It appears in job ads: «se necesita camarero». With several: «se necesitan».
p.prohibido.consejo: The h is silent: pro-i-BI-do. It is very common on signs: «prohibido fumar».
p.aparcar.consejo: In many countries of the Americas they say «estacionar». The c sounds like k: a-par-KAR.
p.entrada.consejo: It has two meanings: the door and the ticket. The context tells you which.
p.cartel.consejo: The stress is at the end: kar-TEL. A sign can be in the street or on a door.
p.fumar.consejo: It is a regular -ar verb. On signs: «prohibido fumar», «no se puede fumar».
b1.texto:
With **se** you can speak of nobody in particular.

- **Passive with se:** what is sold, rented or spoken is the **subject**, and the verb agrees with it: **Se vende** un piso. **Se venden** pisos.
- **Impersonal with se:** there is no subject and the verb stays **singular**: Aquí **se come** muy bien. ¿**Se puede** aparcar? **Se dice** que va a llover.

You will see **Se habla español** on many signs.
b2.f0.texto: Can you park in this street?
b2.f2.texto: But over there they rent out spaces by the hour.
b2.f3.texto: How do you get to the market from here?
b2.f4.texto: You go straight along that street.
b2.f5.texto: They say the food at the market is very good.
b2.f6.texto: And do they sell tickets for the concert?
b2.f7.texto: They are sold at the theatre door from ten o'clock.
b4.texto:
Look at what the verb agrees with:

- With a noun after it, **it agrees with the noun**: se vende **un coche**, se venden **coches**; se habla **español**, se hablan **dos lenguas**.
- With an infinitive or with **que**, the verb is **singular**: se puede **aparcar**, se dice **que** hay una fiesta.
- With an adverb there is no subject: aquí **se come** bien.

Other ways of speaking in general: **ellos** with no subject («dicen que es bueno») or **tú** («si comes bien, vives mejor»).
b4.e1.texto: The food here is very good.
b4.e2.texto: You cannot park in this street.
b5.f0.texto: At dusk, the calm murmur of the fountain can be heard in the square.
b5.f1.texto: In the windows, golden lights come on, one by one.
b5.f2.texto: Above the door of the bar hangs a wooden sign with white letters.
b5.f3.texto: Under the sign you can hear laughter, teaspoons and slow guitar music.
b5.f4.texto: Here people eat slowly and talk calmly, without looking at the clock.
b5.f5.texto: Lucía crosses the square with the map open between her hands.
b5.f6.texto: On the corner they rent out red bicycles with wicker baskets.
b5.f7.texto: A man with big hands explains to her how to get to the river.
b5.f8.texto: She listens attentively and quietly repeats each new word.
b5.f9.texto: In the distance the river can be seen, silvery under the afternoon sun.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Pisos» is plural and it decides: so does the verb.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Vende» is for one thing: «se vende un piso».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Vendo» is «yo vendo»; with «se» the verb is in the third person.
b7.o0.refuerzo: That would be «dices que»; with «se» there is no particular person.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is it! «Se dice» names nobody in particular.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That would be «digo que»; with «se» it is not just me.
b7.pregunta: «Se dice que va a llover.» Who says it?
b8.traduccion: How do you get to the centre
b9.o0.refuerzo: With an infinitive after it, the verb stays singular.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Puedo» is «yo puedo»; with «se» the verb is in the third person.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Well done! With an infinitive there is no subject: «se puede».
b9.pregunta: An infinitive follows. Which verb goes here?
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Se necesita» is what job ads say.
b10.o1.refuerzo: A table is not a waiter.
b10.o2.refuerzo: A customer eats in the bar; the waiter works there.
b10.pregunta: The sign says «Se necesita camarero». What is the bar looking for?
b11.pregunta: Write the sign in Spanish: «Spanish spoken».
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Habitaciones» is plural: the verb must be «alquilan».
b12.o1.refuerzo: Well done! The verb agrees with «habitaciones».
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Habitación» is singular: the verb must be «alquila».
p.alquilan.consejo: «Se alquilan» means something is for rent. The thing rented is plural.
p.plazas.consejo: Here «plazas» means spaces, not a square. The «z» sounds like «th» in Spain.
p.baratas.consejo: Feminine plural, agreeing with «habitaciones». Stress on «RA».
p.doradas.consejo: Feminine plural of «dorado». It describes the lights in the windows.
p.bar.consejo: Like the English word, but in Spanish it is a place for food and drinks.
p.cucharillas.consejo: Little spoons, from «cuchara». The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.lenta.consejo: Feminine of «lento», agreeing with «música». Stress on «LEN».
p.bicicletas.consejo: Plural of «bicicleta». In Spain the «c» before «i» sounds like «th».
p.cestas.consejo: The «c» before «e» sounds like «th» in Spain: «THES-tas».
p.mimbre.consejo: A flexible material from branches, used for baskets and chairs.
p.atenta.consejo: Feminine of «atento», agreeing with «ella». Stress on «TEN».
p.plateado.consejo: From «plata», silver. The stress falls on «A».
p.general.consejo: «En general» means «generally». The «g» before «e» sounds like «h».
